meiji_transition.summary: Sekitetsu and Kamiyama prefectures merged as Ehime in 1873; from 1876 to 1888 it briefly included Sanuki.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Ehime = Iyo Province; the name comes from 'Ehime', the goddess-name of Iyo in the Kojiki (a beautiful maiden).

history_timeline.title: The twin-named island of Iyo
history_timeline.summary: The Kojiki calls Shikoku 'Iyo no Futana-shima', and names Iyo 'Ehime' — the origin of today's prefectural name; Dōgo Onsen appears in the Nihon Shoki.

history_timeline.title: Kōno Michiari and the Mongols
history_timeline.summary: Kōno Michiari of Iyo fought fiercely against the Mongols in 1281 and became famous; Ippen, founder of the Ji sect, was also of the Kōno clan.

history_timeline.title: The Kōno and the Murakami navy
history_timeline.summary: The Kōno held Iyo for generations, while the Murakami navy of the Inland Sea grew powerful, controlling the sea lanes and collecting tolls.

history_timeline.title: The Murakami navy
history_timeline.summary: The missionary Luís Fróis called the Murakami 'the greatest pirates of Japan'; the Kōno ruled central Iyo.

history_timeline.title: The Date of Uwajima
history_timeline.summary: Date Masamune's eldest son Hidemune was given Uwajima; Katō Yoshiaki built Matsuyama Castle, later held by the Matsudaira.

history_timeline.title: Botchan and Shiki
history_timeline.summary: Masaoka Shiki was born in Matsuyama, and Natsume Sōseki set 'Botchan' there; the Shimanami Kaidō (fully opened 2006) links it to Hiroshima.

landmarks.name: Dōgo Onsen Honkan
landmarks.note: One of Japan's oldest hot springs

landmarks.name: Matsuyama Castle
landmarks.note: One of the twelve original keeps

specialties.name: Taimeshi
specialties.note: Uwajima-style raw sea bream over rice

dialect.name: Iyo dialect
dialect.features: A slow, leisurely tone; old Matsuyama's '-zonamoshi' is famous from 'Botchan', and '-ken' is common.

guide.opening: I'm a pilgrim, fresh out of Dōgo Onsen and feeling wonderful. The ships of the Murakami navy once came and went freely on this sea — want to hear some pirate stories?

regional_meme.title: Orange juice from the tap
regional_meme.text: The Ehime legend: turn on the tap and mikan juice comes out — and at Matsuyama Airport it really does.

regional_meme.title: Iyo takes it easy
regional_meme.text: Iyo people speak slowly — 'Iyo nonbiri', the easygoing Iyo — in contrast to the hot-tempered folk of Tosa.

hero_persona.name: Murakami Takeyoshi
hero_persona.title: The greatest pirate in Japan
hero_persona.opening_line: I'm Murakami Takeyoshi, and the Inland Sea is my home! Even the missionaries call me Japan's greatest pirate — any ship passing through pays the toll.
hero_persona.tone_prompt: hearty and bold, a true man of the sea, versed in currents and naval tactics

ramen.highlight: Unlike Nagasaki champon, the broth is clear, Japanese-style and gentle

sake.taste_profile: Rich & sweet: in the sweet-sake tradition of the Inland Sea
